content: For any partner move ABCD -> ABCE, reflection across the perpendicular bisector of AC maps triangle ACD isometrically to triangle CEA. Hence the side multiset and unordered pair of opposite-angle sums are invariant. Fix theta from the first quadrilateral. Every later quadrilateral can be cyclically labeled with opposite-angle sum theta and ordered sides a permutation of the original four. Prove that an ordered side quadruple (w,x,y,z) plus theta determines at most one convex congruence class: if phi is the angle between w,x, equate the two law-of-cosines expressions for the common diagonal. The left side increases strictly with phi while the right side decreases strictly because both relevant angles lie in (0,pi). Convexity fixes the opposite-side gluing of the two determined triangles. Therefore at most 4! congruence classes occur.
Target theorem verified: the answer is no, and any partner sequence has at most 24 congruence classes.
